speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs with regard to home smoke alarms which must be installed in all newly built homes from June 2018 (a) who will be responsible for maintaining the alarms, especially in rental flats, to ensure that the detectors and batteries are working; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider connecting these alarms to a central alert system since many of our elderly have vision and hearing problems and may not notice alerts from the alarms.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: HFADs are standalone devices that are not connected to any central alert system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The purpose of an HFAD is to provide early warning to the occupants in the event of a fire, so that they can quickly extinguish the fire or swiftly make their way to safety before the fire escalates.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) has been encouraging home owners to install HFADs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There are several HFAD models available in the market that cater to different user needs and requirements.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Residents who have vision and hearing problems may consider models with additional features, such as alerts via vibrating pads or visual alarms.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Developers who install such systems should, likewise, be mindful of the needs of their property users.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We note the Member's concern about rental tenants and the elderly.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the Ministry consider instituting maintenance checks as well as battery replacement or repairs for the alarms, especially for rental flats and our studio apartments, given that our elderly may not always know how to check and it may be dangerous for them to do the maintenance check or replace batteries?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I was consulted on this recently and I was told that it will only be installed in the rental flats that have elderly residents, not in all the rental flats.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But then rental flats, people shift in and out, so I would like to ask the Second Minister: will she consider installing in all rental flats?

speaker: Mr Speaker
